::: {.lead}
Today you format a real notice in Word, like in a lab. Each experiment has
two parts. **Part A** is in Word on the lab computer. **Part B** is on a
simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the
screen, click its link. After each step, write your result in its box. At
the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with Word (the desktop app, or Word on the
  web at `office.com`) and the two start files.
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson. Do Part B on your phone.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Formatting and styles

**The idea:** **text formatting** (font, size, bold, colour: **Home ›
Font**) changes only the text that you select. **Paragraph formatting**
(alignment, line spacing: **Home › Paragraph**) changes the whole
paragraph: a click inside it is enough. A **style** is saved formatting
with a name: **Title**, **Heading 1**, **Normal** (Home › Styles); change a
style once, and all the text with it changes. **View › Navigation Pane**
shows the headings as a map.

**Aim:** format one line, and give the headings of a notice their style.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Open `book-fair-start.docx`. In the last line, select only the word
   **free** and click **Bold**. Then click in the same line and click
   **Center**.

   {{< record "Bold changed … ; Center moved …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Bold** changed only the word **free**: text formatting changes only
   the selection. **Center** moved **the whole line**: paragraph formatting
   changes the whole paragraph, and a click inside it is enough.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Only the selected text, or the whole paragraph? Sort the commands.

   Only the selected text (Home › Font)
   :   Bold

       Why: It changes only the letters that you select.

   :   Font size

       Why: A text command: select first.

   :   Font colour

       Why: A text command too.

   The whole paragraph (Home › Paragraph)
   :   Center

       Why: A click inside the line is enough: the whole line moves.

   :   Line spacing

       Why: It changes the space between all the lines of the paragraph.
   :::

2. Give the first line the style **Title** (Home › Styles), and the four
   headings (*When and where*, *What you can bring*, *How to swap a book*,
   *Prices*) the style **Heading 1**.

   {{< record "How do the four headings look now?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Bigger and in a colour (often blue). All four look the same, because
   they have the same style.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   How do the four headings look now?

   - [x] all the same: bigger and in a colour

     Why: They have the same style, Heading 1.

   - [ ] each one a little different

     Why: One style gives the same look to all of them.

   - [ ] like the normal text

     Why: Heading 1 makes them bigger and coloured.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/style-lab.html" poster="sims/style-lab.png" title="Style Lab: styles and the Navigation Pane" >}}

3. In **Style Lab**, give each line its style. How many headings does the
   Navigation Pane show?

   {{< record "The Navigation Pane shows … headings" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **4 headings**: *The plan* and *What to bring* (Heading 1), *Morning*
   and *Afternoon* (Heading 2). The title and the normal text are not in
   the pane.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" unit="headings" hint="Count the lines with Heading 1 or Heading 2."}
   The plan has two lines with Heading 1 and two with Heading 2. How many
   headings does the Navigation Pane show?

   Why: The pane shows the headings only: 2 + 2 = 4. The title and the normal text are not in it.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A table and a picture

**The idea:** a **table** (Insert › Table) puts information in rows and
columns; its first row, the **header row**, names the columns. **Insert ›
Pictures** adds a picture: drag a **corner** to change its size, and choose
**Square** (Layout Options) so that the text flows around it. **Alt text**
says in a few words what the picture shows.

**Aim:** put information in a table, and add a picture.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Under the line *Prices*, insert a table (Insert › Table) of 2 columns
   with a header row: *Book* and *Price (JD)*, then novel 3, dictionary 5
   and notebook 1.

   {{< record "My table has … columns and … rows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 columns and 4 rows**: 1 header row (*Book*, *Price (JD)*) and 3 rows
   for the three items.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="4" unit="rows" hint="One row for the headings, and one row for each item."}
   How many rows does the price table need, with its header row?

   Why: 1 header row + 3 items = 4 rows, in 2 columns: Book and Price (JD).
   :::

2. Click at the start of the text *The college library holds …*. Choose
   **Insert › Pictures › This Device** and open `books.png`. Make it
   smaller with a **corner** handle. Then click **Layout Options** (the
   small button next to the picture) and choose **Square**.

   {{< record "First the picture sits … ; with Square, the text …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   First the picture sits **in the line**, like a very big letter (*In
   Line with Text*). With **Square**, the text **flows around the
   picture**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   With **Square**, what does the text do?

   - [x] It flows around the picture.

     Why: With Square, the picture and the text share the lines.

   - [ ] It moves under the picture.

     Why: That is how a picture in line with the text looks.

   - [ ] It goes behind the picture.

     Why: Square puts the text next to the picture, not behind it.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/list-table-lab.html" poster="sims/list-table-lab.png" title="List and Table Lab: bullets, numbers and a table" >}}

3. In **List and Table Lab**, choose bullets or numbers for each list, then
   build the table of the bus plan. How many columns and rows does the
   table need?

   {{< record "The bus plan: … columns and … rows" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2 columns and 5 rows**: the header row (*Time*, *Activity*) and one
   row for each of the 4 times (9:00, 10:00, 13:00, 16:00).
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5" unit="rows" hint="One header row, and one row for each time."}
   The bus plan has 4 times, each with an activity. How many rows does its
   table need, with the header row?

   Why: 1 header row + 4 times = 5 rows, in 2 columns: Time and Activity.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A draft from AI, checked and proofread

**The idea:** an AI assistant (for example Copilot) writes a **first
draft** fast. You give the facts in the prompt; then you **check** every
line: the AI can add a fact that nobody gave or change a number, and you
delete or fix it. Paste into Word with **Keep Text Only**, then
**proofread**: Review › Spelling & Grammar (F7).

**Aim:** a first draft from AI with only your facts, checked in Word.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the apps (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Copy the prompt into an AI assistant. Find every fact that you did
   **not** give.

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write three short lines for students: the book fair of the college
   library is from Sunday to Tuesday, from 10:00 to 15:00, and entry is
   free.
   :::

   {{< record "Facts that I did not give (or: none)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Your facts: Sunday to Tuesday, 10:00 to 15:00, entry is free. The AI
   often adds something, for example "Every book is 1 JD" or "Writers come
   on Monday": nobody said it, so you delete it.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   The draft has five lines. Keep or delete? Sort them.

   Your fact: keep it
   :   The book fair is from Sunday to Tuesday.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   :   It is open from 10:00 to 15:00.

       Why: You gave the time.

   :   Entry is free.

       Why: You gave this fact.

   Not given: delete it
   :   Every book costs 1 JD.

       Why: Nobody said it: the AI invented it.

   :   Two famous writers come on Monday.

       Why: Not in your prompt: delete it.
   :::

2. Paste the draft at the end of the notice with **Keep Text Only**. Delete
   the facts that you did not give. Then click **Review › Spelling &
   Grammar** (F7).

   {{< record "Spelling & Grammar found … mistakes" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Often **0** or 1. The check finds spelling mistakes, but not a wrong fact
   or a wrong number: only you can check them.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The AI wrote "from 10:00 to 17:00". Does Spelling & Grammar find this
   mistake?

   - [x] no: only you can check the facts and the numbers

     Why: 17:00 is spelled right; it is just not your fact.

   - [ ] yes, it underlines it in red

     Why: Red is for spelling; a wrong number is not a spelling mistake.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/word-ai-lab.html" poster="sims/word-ai-lab.png" title="Word AI Lab: draft, sum up, rewrite, translate" >}}

3. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Sum up** and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and the right fact" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   "Shop staff pick up the price list at **3 pm**": the memo says **5 pm**.
   A summary can change a number, so you find it in the original.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="5 pm|5|5pm|5 p.m.|17:00|5:00 pm" hint="Find the price list in the memo, not in the summary."}
   The summary says: "Shop staff pick up the price list at 3 pm." What time
   does the memo say?

   Why: The memo says 5 pm. A summary can change a number, so you check each one in the original.
   :::
